text: What actually happens when you upload a photo? Let's follow one, end to end.

It starts on the phone. The photo goes to the API gateway, which checks who you are. The upload service gives it a name, and stores the original in object storage — then replies straight away, so you're never left waiting.

text: The slow work happens afterwards, from the stored original. A message goes onto a queue. The thumbnailer picks it up and makes the smaller sizes, and publishes them to the CDN, close to whoever's looking.

text: In code, it's short. Check the user. Store the original. Queue the thumbnails. And reply. Nothing waits on the slow part.

text: Built this way, uploads stay fast, a failed thumbnail is simply retried, and each piece can grow on its own.
